messages:
Sofia M: Heads-up — Tokyo GPU pool has a sustained tokens/sec increase; concurrency up ~28% vs yesterday evening. Seeing longer tails on a few requests. Can we sketch short-term capacity moves?

Amir K: Do we have breakdown by model and seq length? Could be a single customer running long-context jobs.

Sofia M: Quick snapshot from the proxy logs: most of the bump is gen-v2 (1.5x median tokens) and a smaller bump in embeddings. Not all long seqs but more 2-4x than usual.

Jun T: ops-bot just reported infra events: autoscaler started 3 pods, but thermal throttle kicked one GPU into slow mode around 22:04 JST. 

ops-bot: Autoscaler event: added 3 nodes to tokyo-gpu-pool at 2026-11-03T22:05:03Z. Thermal alert: node tok-az1-gpu-12 reduced clocks, migrating pods.

Riley P: Thermal/clocking is worrying — we've seen degraded per-GPU throughput when we hit that sensor threshold. If more nodes warm up they might stabilize but warmup waste will spike GPU hours.

Amir K: Quick numbers I pulled: average tokens/sec per-GPU slid from 18k -> 12.5k during the throttle window. Warmup overhead (startup kernel warmups + model load) added ~3.2 GPU-hours in the last 40m.

Sofia M: Ouch. We need a plan that balances avoiding immediate preemption/overprovision vs not burning credits. Options: 1) force-failover to eu fallback for non-low-latency customers, 2) short-term reserve additional nodes in APAC for peak hours, 3) tune autoscaler to prefer bringing cold nodes earlier to avoid thermal spikes. Thoughts?

Jun T: Suggestion: adjust scaling policy to prefer scale-out by 1-2 nodes earlier at 65% cluster util instead of 80% to smooth headroom. Also add a packing tweak: allow more fractional GPU packing for short jobs to reduce warmup churn.

Riley P: Fractional packing reduces warmup but can increase contention for KV cache; KV hit ratio currently ~0.62 in tokyo during the spike which is already hurting generation latency.

Amir K: If we tilt routing we can send a subset of probabilistic traffic (non-SLA tier) to eu to relieve tokyo by ~10-15% qps. Will that break data locality? Need to check compliance customers.

Sofia M: We have ~7% of traffic flagged as geo-sensitive. We can A/B route 20% of remaining traffic for 30m and measure. If latency stays < target, expand.

Jun T: Cost note: reserve extra nodes for 6 hours will cost ~12 GPU-hours (on-demand equivalent) vs the observed warmup waste of ~3 GPU-hours/hr if we keep oscillating. Net cost depends on stability — likely cheaper to reserve for the peak window.

Riley P: Also consider lowering max-seqlen for non-critical models with a prompt rewrite experiment — 5-10% token reduction there could shave peak tokens/sec meaningfully.

Sofia M: Quick tactical runbook: 1) Amir start routing experiment (20% reroute non-geo traffic to eu). 2) Jun shift autoscaler threshold to 65% and enable early cold-start for 30m window. 3) Riley run a prompt-shortening A/B on fallback clients. 4) Ops monitor: watch tokens/sec, GPU clocks, KV hit rate.

Amir K: On it. Will push routing flux change and mark customers excluded (compliance) in the policy.

Jun T: I'll make the autoscaler change, set cooldown to 3m -> 90s temporarily to speed reaction, and enable fractional packing for <6s jobs only.

Riley P: I'll coordinate with product to pick a safe 8% subset of non-critical traffic for prompt compaction test.

ops-bot: Experiment created: routing-reroute-eu-20pct (id: exp-20261103-01). Autoscaler policy change submitted (id: patch-asc-2764).

Sofia M: Thanks. Follow-ups: check thermal alarms (if repeat, we may need HVAC priority), and reconvene in 45m with a short status. :thumbsup:

Amir K: initial signal: reroute reduced tokyo qps by ~11% within 6m, p50 latency unchanged.

Jun T: Autoscaler brought 2 cold nodes up, but one node still reported clock down; node is marked for maintenance by SRE.

Riley P: Prompt compaction A/B live for 5% so far, initial token reduction ~7% on the cohort.

Sofia M: Good — early signs positive. If thermal recurs after new nodes are warm, we may need to do a capacity purchase for the holiday window. I'll open a brief forecast note with modelling numbers.

Amir K: FYI I'll attach the quick forecast: expected delta if patterns persist: +1200 GPU-hours for the next 7 days at current trend, or +420 GPU-hours if reroute + autoscale smoothing holds.

Jun T: Tagging cost team for heads-up.

Riley P: Filing follow-up action items in the runbook.

Sofia M: Thanks team. Recheck in 45m.
